name: Alexander the Great
cause: when asked to whom his vast empire should belong after his death
last_words: To the strongest.

name: Demosthenes
cause: to Archias of Thurii; Demosthenes had taken poison to avoid arrest by Archias
last_words: Now, as soon as you please you may commence the part of Creon in the tragedy, and cast out this body of mine unburied. But, O gracious Neptune, I, for my part, while I am yet alive, arise up and depart out of this sacred place; though Antipater and the Macedonians have not left so much as thy temple unpolluted.

name: Pompey
cause: to Lucius Septimius, one of his assassins
last_words: Surely I am not mistaken, and you are an old comrade of mine!

name: Julius Caesar
cause: discovering that his stepson Brutus was among his murderers
last_words: You too, my child?

name: Cicero
cause: facing an assassin sent by an enemy
last_words: I go no further: approach, veteran soldier, and, if you can at least do so much properly, sever this neck. [...] What would you have done had you come to me as your first victim?

name: Marcus Junius Brutus
desc: Roman senator and assassin of Julius Caesar
cause: after defeat at the Battle of Philippi. He then bade his friends farewell before killing himself
last_words: By all means must we fly; not with our feet, however, but with our hands.

name: Gaius Cassius Longinus
desc: Roman senator and general, one of Julius Caesar's assassins
cause: erroneously believing his comrade Titinius had been captured by Mark Antony's forces at the Battle of Philippi. Cassius then killed himself
last_words: Through too much fondness of life, I have lived to endure the sight of my friend taken by the enemy before my face.

name: Mark Antony
cause: to Cleopatra before his suicide
last_words: You must not pity me in this last turn of fate. You should rather be happy in the remembrance of our love, and in the recollection that of all men I was once the most famous and the most powerful, and now, at the end, have fallen not dishonorably, a Roman by a Roman vanquished.

name: Cleopatra
cause: right before she reportedly committed suicide by letting an asp bite her
last_words: Here thou art, then!

name: Charmion
cause: when one of Emperor Augustus' men asked her, "Was this well done of your lady, Charmion?" She then fell dead
last_words: Extremely well, and as became the descendant of so many kings.

name: Virgil
last_words: Death twitches my ear. 'Live,' he says. 'I am coming.'

name: Augustus
last_words: Have I played the part well? Then applaud, as I exit.

name: Caligula
cause: after being fatally stabbed
last_words: I am still alive!

name: Agrippina the Younger
cause: to her murderer
last_words: Strike here! Level your rage against the womb which gave birth to such a monster.

name: Lucan
cause: forced to commit suicide after joining in a conspiracy against Nero. He died quoting lines from his own epic poem Pharsalia
last_words: Asunder flies the man- / No single wound the gaping rupture seems, / Where trickling crimson flows the tender streams; / But from an opening horrible and wide / A thousand vessels pour the bursting tide: / At once the winding channel's course was broke, / Where wandering life her mazy journey took.

name: Nero
cause: to a soldier trying to save him after his suicide
last_words: Too late; is this your fidelity?

name: Galba
cause: prior to beheading by supporters of Otho
last_words: Strike, if it be for the Romans' good.

name: Otho
cause: to a freedman, prior to committing suicide
last_words: Go and show yourself to the soldiers, lest they cut you to pieces for being accessory to my death.

name: Vitellius
cause: prior to his killing on the Gemonian stairs
last_words: And yet I was once our emperor.

name: Vespasian
cause: ironically alluding to the Roman practice of posthumously deifying former emperors, before he collapsed and died when attempting to stand up
last_words: Woe, I think I'm turning into a god... An emperor should die on his feet.

name: Titus
last_words: I have made but one mistake.

name: Rabbi Akiva
cause: reciting the Shema Yisrael while being executed by the Romans
last_words: Hear, O Israel! The Lord is our God! The Lord is One!

name: Hadrian
last_words: O my poor soul, whither art thou going?

name: Antoninus Pius
cause: giving the password for the night-watch
last_words: Equanimity.

name: Marcus Aurelius
last_words: Go to the rising sun, for I am setting. Think more of death than of me.

name: Didius Julianus
cause: to his assassin
last_words: But what evil have I done? Whom have I killed?"

name: Septimius Severus
last_words: Hurry, if anything remains for me to do.

name: Saint Lawrence
cause: while being burned alive on a gridiron
last_words: I am roasted,-now turn me, and eat me.

name: Cyprian
desc: Christian bishop of Carthage and martyr
cause: sentenced to death by beheading
last_words: God be thanked.

name: Anthony the Great
last_words: And let my word be kept secret by you, so that no one knows the place but you alone. For in the resurrection of the dead I shall receive my body incorruptible once again from the Savior. Distribute my clothing. To Bishop Athanasius give the one sheepskin and the cloak on which I lie, which he gave to me new, but I have by now worn out. And to Bishop Serapion give the other sheepskin, and you keep the hair garment. And now God preserve you, children, for Antony is leaving and is with you no longer.

name: Cassian of Imola
cause: The pious schoolteacher was sentenced to death by Julian the Apostate and was handed over to his pupils to carry out the deed, which they did by binding him to a stake and stabbing him with their pens.
sources: List of unusual deaths in antiquity

name: Julian
cause: mortally wounded in battle. He had rejected Christianity in favor of paganism; according to some accounts, he was assassinated by a Christian
last_words: And yet Thou hast conquered, O Galilean!

name: Valentinian I
cause: The Roman emperor suffered a stroke which was provoked by yelling at foreign envoys in anger.
sources: List of unusual deaths in antiquity

name: Ambrose
cause: when Simplician was mentioned as his possible successor
last_words: Old though he be, he is the best of all.

name: Martin of Tours
cause: to the Devil
last_words: What dost thou here, thou cruel beast?

name: John Chrysostom
desc: Early Church Father and Archbishop of Constantinople
cause: while traveling deeper into exile
last_words: Glory to God for all things! Amen.

name: Columba
cause: ceasing to transcribe a Psalter
last_words: Here must I stop. What follows, let Baithen write.

name: Phocas
cause: to his successor Heraclius before being executed
last_words: Will you govern it any better?

name: Muhammad
last_words: Oh God, the Friend Most High!" or "The prayer, the prayer! And fear Allah with regard to those whom your right hands possess

name: Goar of Aquitaine
cause: dying in Oberwesel, Austrasia
last_words: Here shall my Saviour be known in all the simplicity of his doctrines. Ah! would that I might witness it; but I have seen those things in a vision. But I faint! I am weary! My earthly journey is finished! Receive my blessing. Go! and be kind one to another.

name: Xuanzang
desc: Chinese Buddhist monk, scholar, traveler and translator
last_words: I desire that whatever merits I may have gained by good works may fall upon other people. May I be born again with them in the heaven of the blessed, be admitted to the family of Mi-le, and serve the Buddha of the future, who is full of kindness and affection. When I descend again upon earth, to pass through other forms of existence, I desire at every new birth to fulfill my duties toward Buddha, and arrive at the end to the highest perfect intelligence.

name: Bede
cause: to a scribe to whom he was dictating a translation of the Gospel of John
last_words: You speak truth, all is finished now. Glory to God.

name: Charlemagne
cause: quoting Jesus
last_words: Lord, into Thy hands I commend my spirit.

name: Louis the Pious
cause: after turning his face to the wall before dying
last_words: Out! out!

name: Louis III of France
cause: The king of West Francia died aged around 18 at Saint-Denis. While mounting his horse to pursue a girl who was running to seek refuge in her father's house, he hit his head on the lintel of a low door and fell, fracturing his skull.
sources: List of unusual deaths in the Middle Ages

name: Basil I
cause: The Byzantine emperor's belt was entangled between antlers of a deer during a hunt and the animal subsequently dragged him for 16 mi through the woods. Because of this accident, Basil contracted fever and he died shortly afterwards.
sources: List of unusual deaths in the Middle Ages

name: Alfred the Great
cause: to his son, Edward the Elder
last_words: Thou my dear son, set thee now beside me, and I will deliver thee true instructions. My son, I feel that my hour is coming. My countenance is wan. My days are almost done. We must now part. I shall to another world, and thou shalt be left alone in all my wealth. I pray thee (for thou art my dear child) strive to be a father, and a lord to thy people. Be thou the children's father, and the widow's friend. Comfort thou the poor, and shelter the weak; and, with all thy might, right that which is wrong. And, son, govern thyself, by law; then shall the Lord love thee, and God above all things shall be thy reward. Call thou upon him to advise thee in all thy need, and so shall he help thee, the better to compass that which thou wouldest.

name: Abd al-Rahman III
last_words: I have now reigned above fifty years in victory or peace; beloved by my subjects, dreaded by my enemies, and respected by my allies. Riches and honors, power and pleasure, have waited on my call, nor does any earthly blessing appear to have been wanting to my felicity. In this situation, I have diligently numbered the days of pure and genuine happiness which have fallen to my lot: they amount to Fourteen:-O man! place not thy confidence in this present world!

name: Hatto II
cause: The archbishop of Mainz is claimed in legend to have been punished for his cruelty to the poor by being eaten alive by rodents.
sources: List of unusual deaths in the Middle Ages

name: Ælfheah of Canterbury
cause: refusing to pay ransom before being killed by his Danish captors
last_words: You urge me in vain. I am not the man to provide Christian flesh for pagan teeth to devour, and it would be so acting if I delivered unto you that which the poor have laid by for their subsistence.

name: Edmund Ironside
cause: According to Henry of Huntington, the English king was stabbed while on a toilet by an assassin hiding underneath.
sources: List of unusual deaths in the Middle Ages

name: Béla I of Hungary
cause: After the Holy Roman Empire decided to launch a military expedition against Hungary to restore his nephew Solomon to the throne, the Hungarian king was seriously injured when "his throne broke beneath him" in his manor at Dömös, later succumbing at a creek near Nagykanizsa.
sources: List of unusual deaths in the Middle Ages

name: Pope Gregory VII
cause: in exile in Salerno due to his conflicts with Henry IV, Holy Roman Emperor
last_words: I have loved justice and hated iniquity; therefore I die in exile.

name: William the Conqueror
cause: after hearing bell ringing Prime
last_words: "I treated the native inhabitants of the kingdom with unreasonable severity, cruelly oppressed high and low, unjustly disinherited many, and caused the death of thousands by starvation and war, especially in Yorkshire....In mad fury I descended on the English of the north like a raging lion, and ordered that their homes and crops with all their equipment and furnishings should be burnt at once and their great flocks and herds of sheep and cattle slaughtered everywhere. So I chastised a great multitude of men and women with the lash of starvation and, alas! was the cruel murderer of many thousands, both young and old, of this fair people.

name: Berengar of Tours
cause: dying in ascetic solitude on the island of Saint-Cosme near Tours
last_words: I shall not long hesitate between conscience and the Pope, for I shall soon appear in the presence of God, to be acquitted, I hope; to be condemned, I fear.

name: William II of England
cause: to Walter Tirel, who allegedly shot the king in a hunting accident
last_words: Shoot, Walter, in the devil's name!

name: Anselm of Canterbury
last_words: Yes, if it be His will, I shall obey it willingly. But were He to let me stay with you a little longer till I have resolved a problem about the origin of the soul, I would gladly accept the boon; for I do not know whether anyone will work it out when I am gone. If I could but eat, I think I should pick up a little strength. I feel no pain in any part of my body; only I cannot retain nourishment, and that exhausts me.

name: Ranulf Flambard
desc: Norman Bishop of Durham and government minister
last_words: I wished to do more harm than I could.

name: Junior KingPhilip of France
cause: The French prince who co-ruled with Louis VI died while riding through Paris when his horse tripped over a black pig that was running out of a dung heap.
sources: List of unusual deaths in the Middle Ages

name: Henry I of England
cause: According to Henry of Huntington, while visiting relatives, the English king ate too many lampreys against his physician's advice, causing a pain in his gut which led to his death.
sources: List of unusual deaths in the Middle Ages

name: Peter Abelard
last_words: I don't know.

name: John II Komnenos
cause: The Byzantine Emperor cut himself with a poisoned arrow during a boar hunt, subsequently dying from sepsis.
sources: List of unusual deaths in the Middle Ages

name: Bernard of Clairvaux
cause: on being told he was dying
last_words: May God's will be done.

name: Pope Adrian IV
cause: The only Englishman to serve as Pope reportedly died after choking on a fly while drinking spring water.
sources: List of unusual deaths in the Middle Ages

name: Eric the Holy
cause: just before being decapitated by his successor Magnus Henriksson
last_words: Let us complete the Service of Offering, the rest of Holy Mass I will celebrate elsewhere!

name: Héloïse
desc: French nun, philosopher, writer, scholar and abbess
last_words: In death at last let me rest with Abelard.

name: Thomas Becket
cause: to his murderers
last_words: For the name of Jesus and the protection of the church I am ready to embrace death.

name: Victims of the Erfurt latrine disaster
cause: While Henry VI, the King of Germany, was holding an informal assembly at the Petersburg Citadel in Erfurt, the combined weight of the assembled nobles caused the wooden second storey floor of the building to collapse. Most of the nobles fell through into the latrine cesspit below the ground floor, where about 60 of them drowned in liquid excrement.
sources: List of unusual deaths in the Middle Ages

name: Andronikos I Komnenos
cause: lynched by his former subjects
last_words: Lord, have mercy upon me. Wilt thou break a bruised reed?

name: Henry II of England
cause: on being told his son John was one of those conspiring against him
last_words: Now let the world go as it will; I care for nothing more.

name: Frederick Barbarossa
cause: While leading the German army on the Third Crusade, the Holy Roman Emperor unexpectedly drowned while bathing in the Saleph.
sources: List of unusual deaths in the Middle Ages

name: Saladin
desc: first sultan of Egypt and Syria
last_words: When I am buried, carry my winding-sheet on the point of a spear, and say these words: Behold the spoils which Saladin carries with him! Of all his victories, realms, and riches, nothing remains to him but this.

name: Richard I of England
cause: with reference to the young man who had mortally wounded him with a crossbow
last_words: Youth, I forgive thee! Take off his chains, give him 100 shillings, and let him go.

name: Saint Dominic
desc: Castilian Catholic priest, founder of the Dominican Order, when asked where he wanted to be buried
last_words: Under the feet of my friars.

name: Francis of Assisi
last_words: I have sinned against my brother, the ass.

name: Genghis Khan
last_words: Let not my end disarm you, and on no account weep or keen for me, lest the enemy be warned of my death.

name: Anthony of Padua
desc: Portuguese Catholic priest and Franciscan friar
last_words: I see my God. He calls me to Him.

name: Skule Bårdsson
cause: before being killed by supporters of King Haakon IV of Norway
last_words: Don't cut my face.

name: Enguerrand III, Lord of Coucy
cause: The French nobleman died at 60 years of age when, during a rough ride, he fell off his horse and impaled himself on his own sword.
sources: List of unusual deaths in the Middle Ages

name: Gruffudd ap Llywelyn ab Iorwerth
cause: The first-born son of Llywelyn the Great died while attempting to lower himself from the Tower of London in an escape attempt. The rope, made out of sheets and other fabrics, snapped, and his neck was broken in the fall, according to English monk and chronicler, Matthew Paris.
sources: List of unusual deaths in the Middle Ages

name: Al-Musta'sim
cause: The last Abbasid Caliph of Baghdad was executed by his Mongol captors by being rolled up in a rug and then trampled by horses.
sources: List of unusual deaths in the Middle Ages

name: Simon de Montfort, 6th Earl of Leicester
cause: before dying at the Battle of Evesham
last_words: By the arm of St. James, it is time to die.

name: Conradin
desc: last direct heir of the House of Hohenstaufen
cause: prior to execution by beheading at the age of 16
last_words: O my mother! how deep will be thy sorrow at the news of this day!

name: Louis IX of France
last_words: I will enter thy house. I will worship in Thy sanctuary.

name: Thomas Aquinas
cause: as he received his last rites
last_words: I have written and taught much about this very holy Body, and about the other sacraments in the faith of Christ, and about the Holy Roman Church, to whose correction I expose and submit everything I have written.

name: Rudolf I of Germany
cause: he was buried at Speyer Cathedral
last_words: I am on the way to Spires to visit the kings, my predecessors.

name: Edward I of England
cause: to his son, Edward II of England, while dying during a war with Scotland
last_words: Carry my bones before you on your march, for the rebels will not be able to endure the sight of me, alive or dead.

name: Jacques de Molay
desc: last Grand Master of the Knights Templar
cause: before being burned at the stake
last_words: Pope Clement, Chevalier Guillaume de Nogaret, King Philip! I summon you to the Tribunal of Heaven before the year is out!

name: Thomas, 2nd Earl of Lancaster
cause: before beheading for treason against his cousin, Edward II of England
last_words: King of heaven, do thou have mercy on me, for the king of earth hath forsaken me.

name: Marco Polo
cause: responding to skepticism about the content of his memoir, The Travels of Marco Polo
last_words: I have not told half of what I saw.

name: Edward II of England
cause: The English king was rumoured to have been murdered after being deposed and imprisoned by his wife Isabella and her lover Roger Mortimer, by having a horn pushed into his anus through which a red-hot iron was inserted, burning out his internal organs without marking his body. However, there is no real academic consensus on the manner of Edward II's death, and it has been plausibly argued that the story is propaganda.
sources: List of unusual deaths in the Middle Ages

name: Edward the Black Prince
last_words: I give thee thanks, O God, for all thy benefits, and with all the pains of my soul I humbly beseech thy mercy to give me remission of those sins I have wickedly committed against thee; and of all mortal men whom willingly or ignorantly I have offended, with all my heart I desire forgiveness.

name: Edward III of England
cause: kissing a crucifix
last_words: Jesus.

name: Charles V of France
last_words: Ah, Jesus!

name: Wat Tyler
cause: prior to being killed by officers loyal to Richard II of England
last_words: Because they are all under my command, they are sworn to do what I bid them.

name: Charles II of Navarre
cause: The contemporary chronicler Froissart relates that the king of Navarre, known as "Charles the Bad", suffering from illness in old age, was ordered by his physician to be tightly sewn into a linen sheet soaked in distilled spirits. The highly flammable sheet accidentally caught fire, and he later died of his injuries.
sources: List of unusual deaths in the Middle Ages

name: Gaston III, Count of Foix
last_words: I am a dead man! Lord, have mercy upon me!

name: Timur
desc: Turco-Mongol conqueror, founder of the Timurid Empire
last_words: Never yet has death been frightened away by screaming.

name: Martin of Aragon
cause: The Aragonese king died from a combination of indigestion and uncontrollable laughing. According to legend, Martin was suffering from indigestion, caused by eating an entire goose, when his favorite jester, Borra, entered the king's bedroom. When Martin asked Borra where he had been, the jester replied with: "Out of the next vineyard, where I saw a young deer hanging by his tail from a tree, as if someone had so punished him for stealing figs." This joke caused the king to die from laughter.
sources: List of unusual deaths in the Renaissance

name: Margaret
desc: Queen of Denmark, Norway and Sweden
cause: afflicted with the plague in Flensburg harbor
last_words: We are now to sail home, at once!

name: Jan Hus
cause: While being burned at the stake for heresy, he saw an old woman throw a small amount of brushwood onto the fire
last_words: O, holy simplicity!

name: Jerome of Prague
cause: burned for heresy
last_words: O Lord God, Father Almighty, have mercy upon me, and be merciful unto mine offences, for thou knowest how sincerely I have loved Thy truth.

name: Jan Žižka
last_words: Make my skin into drumheads for the Bohemian cause.

name: Joan of Arc
cause: while she was burning at the stake
last_words: Hold the cross high so I may see it through the flames!

name: Margaret Stewart, Dauphine of France
last_words: Fie on life! Speak no more of it to me.

name: Henry Beaufort
cause: Cardinal, Bishop of Winchester
last_words: Will not all my riches save me? What, is there no bribing death?

name: Sejong the Great
cause: Korea would later be invaded and pillaged by the Japanese, and later, subjugated by the Manchus, who the Koreans considered 'barbarians'
last_words: Although dealing with the Japanese and the barbarians is not something that should be taken lightly, I fear that as peace is ingrained in you, the days growing longer, all matters might be done lazily and slowly, so you should always be careful and watch out every day, so you do not give in to negligence.

name: Constantine XI
cause: Byzantine Empire, before charging into Ottoman lines during the Fall of Constantinople, he was never seen again
last_words: God forbid that I should live as an Emperor without an Empire. As my city falls, I will fall with it. Whosoever wishes to escape, let him save himself if he can, and whoever is ready to face death, let him follow me.

name: John II of Castile
cause: King of Castile
last_words: Were I born the son of a farmer, and became a friar of the Abrojo, and not the king of Castile.

name: George Plantagenet, Duke of Clarence
cause: The 1st Duke of Clarence was allegedly executed by drowning in a barrel of Malmsey wine, apparently his own choice once he accepted he was to be killed.
sources: List of unusual deaths in the Renaissance

name: Louis XI
last_words: Our Lady of Embrun, my good mistress, help me.

name: Richard III of England
cause: when deserted by his best troops at the Battle of Bosworth Field
last_words: Treason! treason!

name: Wessel Gansfort
last_words: I know only Jesus the crucified.

name: Girolamo Savonarola
cause: when asked before his execution if he was resigned to death
last_words: My Lord died innocent of all crimes, for my sins; and shall not I willingly give my soul for the love of Him.

name: Charles VIII of France
cause: The French king died as a result of striking his head on the lintel of a door while on his way to watch a game of real tennis.
last_words: I hope never again to commit a mortal sin, nor even a venial one, if I can help it.
sources: List of unusual deaths in the Renaissance

name: Pope Alexander VI
last_words: All right, all right, I'm coming. Wait a moment.

name: Christopher Columbus
cause: quoting Jesus
last_words: Into Your hands, O Lord, I commend my spirit.

name: Henry VII of England
last_words: We heartily desire our executors to consider how behoofful it is to be prayed for.

name: Georges d'Amboise
desc: French Roman Catholic cardinal and minister of state
last_words: I believe.

name: Leonardo da Vinci
cause: to King Francis I of France
last_words: I have offended God and mankind because my work did not reach the quality it should have.

name: Moctezuma II
desc: Huey Tlatoani or Emperor of the Aztec Empire
cause: to Hernán Cortés (calling him by the name of his interpreter, La Malinche)
last_words: I confide to your care my beloved children, the most precious jewels I can leave you. The great monarch beyond the ocean will interest himself to see that they come into their inheritance, if you present before him their just claims. I know your master will do this, if for no other reason, then for the kindness I have shown the Spaniards, though it has occasioned my ruin. For all my misfortunes, Malinche, I bear you no ill will.

name: Raphael
last_words: Happy.

name: Pope Leo X
cause: rumored to have died by poison
last_words: I have been murdered; no remedy can prevent my speedy death.

name: Franz von Sickingen
cause: when his chaplain asked if he wanted to confess prior to his death defending his castle
last_words: I have already confessed my sins to God.

name: Pierre Terrail, seigneur de Bayard
cause: mortally wounded at the Battle of the Sesia (1524)
last_words: At least I may die facing the enemy.

name: Niccolò Machiavelli
cause: Italian Renaissance diplomat, philosopher and writer
last_words: I desire to go to hell, and not to heaven. In the former place I shall enjoy the company of popes, kings, and princes, while in the latter are only beggars, monks, hermits, and apostles.

name: Patrick Hamilton
cause: while being burned at the stake
last_words: How long, Lord, shall darkness cover this land? How long wilt thou suffer this tyranny of men? Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.

name: Babur
desc: founder of the Mughal Empire and first Emperor of the Mughal dynasty
last_words: I give your brothers to your keeping. Be faithful to them and all the people.

name: Thomas Wolsey
cause: to the Lieutenant of the Tower of London, after falling ill on the way to London under arrest for treason
last_words: And, Master Kyngston, had I but served God as diligently as I have served the king, he would not have given me over in my gray hairs. But this is my just reward for my pains and study, not regarding my service to God, but only my duty to my Prince.

name: Huldrych Zwingli
desc: priest and leader of the Reformation in Switzerland
cause: mortally wounded at the Battle of Kappel
last_words: Can this be considered a calamity? Well! they can, indeed, kill the body, but they are not able to kill the soul.

name: Thomas Bilney
cause: While he awaited burning for heresy, the friars and people present argued over who was responsible for Bilney's death; the friars threatened to withhold alms from the people if they were blamed
last_words: I pray you, good people, be not the worse to these men on my account, as though they were the authors of my death.

name: William Warham
cause: when a servant told him he had thirty pounds left
last_words: That is enough to last till I get to Heaven.

name: James Bainham
cause: while burning at the stake for heresy
last_words: O ye papists: behold, ye look for miracles, and here now ye may see a miracle, for in this fire I feel no more pain than if I were in a bed of down, but it is to me as sweet as a bed of roses.

name: Atahualpa
desc: last Sapa Inca of the Inca Empire
cause: prior to execution by strangling
last_words: What have I done, or my children, that I should meet such a fate? And from your hands, too, you who have met with friendship and kindness from my people who have received nothing but benefits from my hands.

name: Ludovica Albertoni
desc: Italian noblewoman, professed member of the Third Order of Saint Francis
cause: quoting Jesus
last_words: Father, into Thy hands I commend my spirit.

name: Ludovico Ariosto
last_words: This is not my home.

name: Heinrich Cornelius Agrippa
cause: to his black dog (allegedly his familiar)
last_words: Begone thou wretched beast, which hast utterly undone me.

name: Thomas More
cause: prior to beheading for treason
last_words: I die the King's good servant, and God's first.

name: Erasmus
desc: Dutch Catholic priest and humanist scholar
last_words: Lord! Lord! make an end! make an end!

name: Robert Pakington
cause: The 47-year-old merchant and MP was killed in London by a wheellock pistol, making his death the first political assassination performed by a firearm.
sources: List of unusual deaths in the Renaissance

name: Mark Smeaton
desc: musician in the household of Queen Anne Boleyn
cause: prior to beheading for alleged treason and adultery
last_words: Masters, I pray you pray for me, for I have deserved this death.

name: Anne Boleyn
cause: prior to her execution by beheading
last_words: Oh God, have pity on my soul. Oh God, have pity on my soul.

name: William Tyndale
cause: before being strangled and burned at the stake for heresy
last_words: Lord, open the King of England's eyes.

name: Catherine of Aragon
cause: closing her last letter to her former husband, Henry VIII of England
last_words: Mine eyes desire thee only. Farewell.

name: Filippo Strozzi the Younger
cause: He carved this line from Virgil's Aeneid on a mantelpiece with his sword as his suicide note
last_words: May an avenger arise from my bones.

name: John Lambert
cause: while being burned at the stake
last_words: None but Christ! None but Christ!

name: Thomas Forret

He was dragged around the walls with sacks of earth and stone on his back; next, he was tied to a chair and hoisted to the yardarm of the Turkish flagship, where he was exposed to the taunts of the sailors. Finally, he was taken to his place of execution in the main square, tied naked to a column, and flayed alive. Bragadin's skin was stuffed with straw and sewn, reinvested with his military insignia, and exhibited riding an ox in a mocking procession along the streets of Famagusta. The macabre trophy was hoisted upon the masthead pennant of the personal galley of the Ottoman commander, Amir al-bahr Mustafa Pasha, to be taken to Constantinople as a gift for Sultan Selim II. Bragadin's skin was stolen in 1580 by a Venetian seaman and brought back to Venice, where it was received as a returning hero.

name: James Sharp
last_words: I shall be happy.

name: Thomas Hobbes
last_words: Now I am about to take my last voyage, a great leap in the dark.

name: Thomas Blood
last_words: I do not fear death.

name: John Wilmot, 2nd Earl of Rochester
last_words: The only objection against the Bible is a bad life.

name: William Howard, 1st Viscount Stafford
cause: to his executioner prior to beheading for alleged treason
last_words: I do forgive you.

name: William Russell, Lord Russell
cause: after bidding farewell to his wife prior to execution by beheading for treason
last_words: Now the bitterness of death is past.

name: John Owen
desc: English Nonconformist church leader and theologian
cause: when his secretary had written "I am still in the land of the living" in a letter in his name
last_words: Stop. Change that to say, 'I am yet in the land of the dying, but I hope soon to be in the land of the living.'

name: Algernon Sidney
cause: prior to execution by beheading for treason
last_words: I know that my Redeemer liveth. I die for the good old cause.

name: James Scott, 1st Duke of Monmouth
desc: illegitimate son of Charles II of England
cause: to Jack Ketch, his executioner. Ketch was nervous and took several blows to behead Scott
last_words: There are six guineas for you, and do not hack me as you did my Lord Russell. I have heard that you struck him three or four times. My servant will give you more gold if you do your work well.

name: Wentworth Dillon, 4th Earl of Roscommon
desc: Anglo-Irish landlord, Irish peer, and poet
cause: quoting from his own translation of the "Dies irae"
last_words: My God, my Father, and my Friend, / Do not forsake me in the end.

name: Charles II of England
last_words: I have been a most unconscionable time dying, but I beg you to excuse it.

name: Jean-Baptiste Lully
cause: The French composer died of a gangrenous abscess after accidentally piercing his foot with a staff while he was vigorously conducting a Te Deum. It was customary at that time to conduct by banging a staff on the floor. He refused to have his leg amputated so he could still dance.
sources: List of unusual deaths in the early modern period

name: James Renwick
cause: before execution by hanging
last_words: Lord, into Thy hands I commend my spirit; for Thou hast redeemed me, Lord God of truth.

name: John Bunyan
last_words: Take me, for I come to Thee.

name: Margaret Mary Alacoque
desc: French Roman Catholic nun, promoter of devotion to the Sacred Heart of Jesus
last_words: I need nothing but God, and to lose myself in the heart of Jesus.

name: John Eliot
desc: Puritan missionary to the American Indians, founder of Roxbury Latin School
last_words: O, come in glory! I have long waited for Thy coming. Let no dark cloud rest on the work of the Indians. Let it live when I am dead. Welcome joy!

name: George Fox
desc: English Dissenter, founder of the Religious Society of Friends
last_words: Never heed; the Lord's power is over all weakness and death.

name: John Flavel
last_words: I know that it will be well with me.

name: Richard Baxter
desc: English Puritan church leader, poet, hymnodist and theologian
last_words: Death, death. O I thank Him, I thank Him. The Lord teach you to die.

name: Giles Corey
cause: before being pressed to death during the Salem witch trials
last_words: More weight.

name: Sarah Good
desc: American woman accused of witchcraft during the Salem witch trials
cause: to Reverend Nicholas Noyes prior to execution by hanging
last_words: You are a lyer; I am no more a Witch than you are a Wizard, and if you take away my Life, God will give you Blood to drink.

name: Patrick Sarsfield, 1st Earl of Lucan
cause: mortally wounded at the Battle of Landen
last_words: Oh, that this were for Ireland.

name: Ulrica Eleanor the Elder
cause: to her husband holding her
last_words: Yes, like that, just like that, my royal friend, raise me upward, upward!

name: Mary II of England
cause: when the clergyman reading the prayers for the sick paused due to being overcome by grief
last_words: My Lord, why do you not go on? I am not afraid to die.

name: Suleiman I of Persia
cause: According to the French cleric, Martin Gaudereau
last_words: Bring me wine.

name: Philip Henry
cause: quoting 1 Corinthians 15:55
last_words: O death, where is thy-

name: Hortense Mancini
desc: Duchesse de Mazarin, niece of Cardinal Mazarin and mistress of Charles II of England
cause: dying in financial ruin
last_words: Debt!

name: Charles II of Spain
last_words: I am nothing.

name: James II of England
cause: in reply to Louis XIV telling him that he would acknowledge James' son, James Francis Edward Stuart, as King of England, Scotland and Ireland
last_words: Grateful - in peace!

name: Asano Naganori
desc: daimyō of the Akō Domain in Japan
cause: death poem for his seppuku
last_words: I wish I could enjoy / the rest of Spring / as the cherry blossoms are yet in bloom / in spite of the spring breeze / which is attempting to blow off all their petals.

name: Dominique Bouhours
last_words: I am about to-or I am going to-die; either expression is correct.

name: William III of England
cause: dying of pneumonia after breaking his collarbone, to his physician The king of England was riding his horse when it stumbled on a molehill. William fell and broke his collarbone, then contracted pneumonia and died several days later. After he died, Jacobites were said to have toasted in the mole's honour, calling it "the little gentleman in the black velvet waistcoat".
last_words: Can this last long?
sources: List of unusual deaths in the early modern period

name: Hannah Twynnoy
cause: The 33-year-old barmaid at the White Lion Inn was mauled to death by a tiger in Malmesbury, Wiltshire. She was the first person to be killed by a tiger in British history.
sources: List of unusual deaths in the early modern period

name: Charles de Saint-Évremond
cause: when a clergyman asked if he would be reconciled
last_words: With all my heart: I would fain be reconciled to my stomach, which no longer performs its usual functions.

name: Jacques-Bénigne Bossuet
last_words: Thy will be done.

name: John Locke
last_words: ...in perfect charity with all men and in sincere communion with the whole church of Christ, by whatever name Christ's followers call themselves.

name: Titus Oates
desc: English priest and perjurer, fabricator of the "Popish Plot"
last_words: It is all the same in the end.

name: Leopold I, Holy Roman Emperor
last_words: Let me die to the sound of sweet music.

name: George Farquhar
cause: to his friend Robert Wilks
last_words: Dear Bob, I have nothing to leave thee to perpetuate my memory but two helpless girls. Look upon them sometimes, and think of him who was to the last moment of his life thine, George Farquhar.

name: Aurangzeb
cause: in a letter to his youngest son, Muhammad Kam Bakhsh
last_words: Wherever I look I see nothing but the Divinity.-I have committed numerous crimes and I know not with what punishments I may be seized.-The agonies of death come upon me fast.-I am going. Whatever good or evil I have done, it was for you. No one has seen the departure of his own soul; but I know that mine is departing.

name: Marcello d'Aste
last_words: I wish to die sitting, in tribute to the most worshipful will of my good and precious Jesus.

name: Nicolas Boileau-Despréaux
cause: to a playwright who asked him to read his new play
last_words: Do you wish to hasten my last hour?

name: Thomas Ken
last_words: God's will be done.

name: Thomas Halyburton
last_words: Pray, pray!

name: Juraj Jánošík
desc: Slovak highwayman known as "the Slovak Robin Hood"
cause: refusing to name fellow robbers prior to jumping onto the hook on which he was to be hung
last_words: If you have baked me so you also should eat me!

name: Anne, Queen of Great Britain
cause: handing the Lord High Treasurer's staff of office to Charles Talbot, 1st Duke of Shrewsbury
last_words: Use it for the good of my people.

name: Matthew Henry
last_words: A life spent in the service of God, and communion with Him, is the most comfortable and pleasant life that any one can live in this present world.

name: Louis XIV
last_words: I'm going, but the State will always remain.

name: François Fénelon
desc: French Roman Catholic archbishop, theologian and writer
cause: quoting Jesus
last_words: Not my will, but thine be done.

name: William Wycherley
cause: to his wife. He had married a much younger woman less than twelve days before his death
last_words: Promise me you will never again marry an old man.

name: William Penn
desc: English writer and religious thinker, founder of the Province of Pennsylvania
last_words: To be like Christ is to be a Christian.

name: Charles XII
cause: when stepping down from his perch into an entrenchment just as he was shot in the head
last_words: I am coming down now.

name: Joseph Addison
cause: to his stepson, Edward Rich, 7th Earl of Warwick
last_words: See in what peace a Christian can die.

name: George Smalridge
last_words: God be thanked, I have had a very good night.

name: Increase Mather
desc: New England Puritan clergyman, president of Harvard College
last_words: Be fruitful.

name: Jack Sheppard
cause: prior to execution by hanging
last_words: I have ever cherished an honest pride; never have I stooped to friendship with Jonathan Wild, or with any of his detestable thief-takers; and though an undutiful son, I never damned my mother's eyes.

name: Jonathan Wild
cause: prior to execution by hanging
last_words: Lord Jesus, receive my soul!

name: Isaac Newton
last_words: I don't know what I may seem to the world. But as to myself I seem to have been only like a boy playing on the seashore and diverting myself now and then in finding a smoother pebble or a prettier shell than the ordinary, whilst the great ocean of truth lay all undiscovered before me.

name: August Hermann Francke
cause: when his wife asked if his Savior was still with him
last_words: Yes.

name: Cotton Mather
desc: New England Puritan minister and author
cause: His wife wiped his eyes with her handkerchief as he said the last words, alluding to Revelation 21:4
last_words: Is this dying? Is this all? Is this all that I feared when I prayed against a hard death? Oh! I can bear this! I can bear it! I can bear it! I am going where all tears will be wiped from my eyes.

name: Anthony Collins
last_words: I have always endeavored, to the best of my ability, to serve God, my king and my country. I go to the place God has designed for those who love him.

name: Sally Basset
cause: looking at the logs prepared to fuel her burning at the stake for poisoning
last_words: Ain't they darlin'?

name: Matthew Tindal
last_words: O God-if there be a God-I desire Thee to have mercy on me.

name: Thomas Woolston
cause: dying while imprisoned for blasphemy
last_words: This is a struggle which all men must go through, and which I bear not only with patience, but with willingness.

name: Thomas Fantet de Lagny
cause: responding to the question "What is the square of 12?" on his deathbed
last_words: One hundred and forty-four.

name: Rob Roy MacGregor
last_words: Now all is over-let the piper play Ha til mi tulidh [we return no more].

name: Eustace Budgell
cause: his suicide note, written before drowning himself in the Thames. Joseph Addison was Budgell's cousin
last_words: What Cato did, and Addison approved, cannot be wrong.

name: Turlough O'Carolan
desc: Irish Celtic harper, composer and singer
cause: to a bowl of wine he was no longer able to drink
last_words: It would be hard indeed if we two dear friends should part after so many years, without one sweet kiss.

name: Frederick William I of Prussia
desc: King in Prussia and Elector of Brandenburg
cause: in response to priest or family members quoting Job 1:21
last_words: No, not quite naked. I shall have my uniform on.

name: Andrew Bradford
last_words: Oh Lord! Forgive the errata!

name: Richard Savage
cause: unable to remember what he wanted to say to his keeper at Bristol Newgate Prison. The keeper found Savage dead the next morning
last_words: I have something to say to you, sir... 'Tis gone.

name: Alexander Pope
last_words: I am dying, sir, of a hundred good symptoms.

name: Jonathan Swift
cause: referring to George Frideric Handel, who had come to visit him
last_words: Ah! A German and a genius! A prodigy-admit him!

name: James Gardiner
cause: to a Jacobite officer after being mortally wounded at the Battle of Prestonpans
last_words: You are fighting for an earthly crown; I am going to receive a heavenly one.

name: Simon Fraser, 11th Lord Lovat
cause: quoting a line of Horace when executed by beheading as a Jacobite rebel
last_words: Dulce et decorum est pro patria mori.

name: David Brainerd
desc: American missionary to the Native Americans
cause: quoting Luke 2:29
last_words: Lord, now let thy servant depart in peace.

name: Isaac Watts
desc: English Christian minister, hymn writer and theologian
last_words: Waiting God's leave to die.

name: Johann Sebastian Bach
last_words: Don't cry for me, for I go where music is born.

name: Henry St John, 1st Viscount Bolingbroke
cause: to Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield. Bolingbroke also reaffirmed his Deist convictions
last_words: God, who pleased me here, will do what he pleases with me hereafter, and he knows best what to do. May he bless you.

name: Frederick, Prince of Wales
cause: The son of George II of Great Britain and father of George III died of a pulmonary embolism, but was commonly claimed to have been killed by being struck by a cricket ball.
sources: List of unusual deaths in the early modern period

name: Joseph Butler
cause: referring to John 6:37
last_words: I have often read and thought of that scripture, but never till this moment did I feel its full power, and now I die happy.

name: Mary Blandy
cause: prior to execution by hanging
last_words: For the sake of decency, gentlemen, don't hang me high.

name: Richard Newton
last_words: Christ Jesus the Saviour of sinners and life of the dead. I am going, going to Glory! Farewell sin! Farewell death! Praise the Lord!

name: Professor Georg Wilhelm Richmann
cause: The Russian physicist was killed when a globe of ball lightning which he created in his laboratory struck him in the forehead.
sources: List of unusual deaths in the early modern period

name: Henry Hall
cause: The 94-year-old British lighthouse keeper died several days after fighting a fire at Rudyerd's Tower, during which molten lead from the roof fell down his throat. His autopsy revealed that "the diaphragmatic upper mouth of the stomach greatly inflamed and ulcerated, and the tuncia in the lower part of the stomach burnt; and from the great cavity of it took out a great piece of lead ... which weighed exactly seven ounces, five drachms and eighteen grains". The piece of lead is currently in the collection of the National Museum of Scotland.
sources: List of unusual deaths in the early modern period

name: Robert-François Damiens
desc: French domestic servant, attempted assassin of Louis XV
cause: during execution by dismemberment
last_words: O death, why art thou so long in coming?

name: Kurt Christoph Graf von Schwerin
cause: just before being fatally struck by enemy fire at the Battle of Prague (1757)
last_words: Let all brave Prussians follow me!

name: Bernard Le Bovier de Fontenelle
cause: dying at the age of 99
last_words: I do not suffer, my friends; I only feel a certain difficulty of living.

name: Jonathan Edwards
cause: when someone lamented what his loss would mean to the church and to the College of New Jersey
last_words: Trust in God and you need not fear.

name: James Hervey
last_words: Precious salvation!

name: Pope Benedict XIV
last_words: Sic transit gloria mundi.

name: William Webster
desc: British priest in the Church of England and theological writer
last_words: Peace.

name: James Wolfe
cause: mortally wounded at the Battle of the Plains of Abraham, on learning that the French forces were fleeing
last_words: Go, one of you, to Colonel Burton; tell him to march Webb's regiment down to Charles River, to cut off their retreat from the bridge. Now, God be praised, I will die in peace!

name: Louis-Joseph de Montcalm
cause: on being told the wound he had received at the Battle of the Plains of Abraham was mortal
last_words: So much the better. I am happy that I shall not live to see the surrender of Quebec. I have much business that must be attended to of greater moment than your ruined garrison and this wretched country.

name: Eugene Aram
cause: when asked if he had anything to say before hanging
last_words: No.

name: Nicolaus Zinzendorf
desc: German religious and social reformer and bishop of the Moravian Church
cause: to his son-in-law
last_words: Now, my dear son, I am going to the Saviour. I am ready; I am quite resigned to the will of my Lord. If He is no longer willing to make use of me here I am quite ready to go to Him, for there is nothing more in my way.

name: Mary Wortley Montagu
last_words: It has all been most interesting.

name: Jean-Philippe Rameau
cause: to his confessor
last_words: What the devil do you mean to sing to me, priest? You are out of tune.

name: Madame de Pompadour
desc: chief mistress of Louis XV of France
cause: applying rouge to her cheeks before her death
last_words: Wait a second.

name: François-Jean de la Barre
cause: prior to execution by beheading for blasphemy and sacrilege
last_words: I did not think that they would put a young gentleman to death for such a trifle.

name: Frederick V of Denmark
last_words: It is a great consolation to me, in my last hour, that I have never wilfully offended anyone, and that there is not a drop of blood on my hands.

name: James Quin
cause: English actor
last_words: I could wish this tragic scene were over, but I hope to go through it with becoming dignity.

name: Stanisław Leszczyński
cause: The duke of Lorraine and former king of Poland died from wounds after his silk attire had caught fire from a spark while he was sitting near the fireplace in his Château de Lunéville.
sources: List of unusual deaths in the early modern period

name: Laurence Sterne
last_words: Now it has come.

name: Christian Fürchtegott Gellert
cause: on being told he had only an hour to live
last_words: Now, God be praised, only one hour!

name: George Whitefield
cause: to a servant
last_words: I am dying.

name: Louis Petit de Bachaumont
last_words: The priest could never draw another thing from dying but 'Dear Sir, you are so kind.'

name: Thomas Gray
last_words: Molly, I shall die!

name: Thomas Rutherforth
last_words: He has indeed been a precious Christ to me; and now I feel him to be my rock, my strength, my rest, my hope, my joy, my all in all.

name: Emanuel Swedenborg
desc: Swedish theologian, scientist, philosopher and mystic
last_words: What o'clock is it?" (On being told) "It is well; I thank you; God bless you.

name: Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield
cause: asking a servant to seat his godson, Solomon Dayrolles
last_words: Give Dayrolles a chair.

name: John Day
cause: The English carpenter and wheelwright was the first human known to have died in an accident with a submarine. Day submerged himself in Plymouth Sound in a wooden diving chamber attached to a sloop named the Maria and never resurfaced.
sources: List of unusual deaths in the early modern period

name: Oliver Goldsmith
cause: in response to his physician asking if his mind was at ease
last_words: No, it is not.

name: Joseph Warren
cause: mortally wounded at the Battle of Bunker Hill
last_words: I am a dead man: fight on, my brave fellows, for the salvation of your country.

name: Richard Montgomery
desc: Irish soldier, major general in the Continental Army
cause: killed at the Battle of Quebec (1775)
last_words: What news from Boston?

name: Ludwig Christoph Heinrich Hölty
last_words: I am very ill. Send for Zimmermann. In fact, I think I'll die today.

name: William Battie
cause: to his caretaker
last_words: Young man, you have heard, no doubt, how great are the terrors of death. This night will probably afford you some experience; but you may learn, and may you profit by the example, that a conscientious endeavor to perform his duty through life will ever close a Christian's eyes with comfort and tranquility!

name: Nathan Hale
cause: before being hanged by the British for his involvement in the American Revolutionary War
last_words: I only regret that I have but one life to give for my country.

name: Albrecht von Haller
cause: to his friend Dr. Rosselet
last_words: My friend, the artery ceases to beat.

name: William Dodd
desc: English Anglican clergyman and man of letters
cause: to his executioner prior to hanging for forgery. He then whispered something unknown to the executioner
last_words: Come to me.

name: Augustus Toplady
desc: Anglican cleric and hymn writer, author of "Rock of Ages"
last_words: No mortal man can live after the glories which God has manifested to my soul.

name: Anne Steele
desc: English Baptist hymn writer and essayist
cause: quoting Job 19:25
last_words: I know that my Redeemer liveth.

name: Jean-Jacques Rousseau
last_words: Throw up the window that I may see once more the magnificent scene of nature.

name: Voltaire
cause: when asked by a priest to renounce Satan before his death
last_words: Now is not the time for making new enemies.

name: Nicholas Biddle
cause: wounded in battle between USS Randolph and HMS Yarmouth. While the surgeon was treating Biddle, the Randolph exploded, killing all but four crewmembers
last_words: Bring me a chair; carry me forward; and there the surgeon will dress my wound.

name: James Cook
desc: British explorer and Royal Navy captain
cause: after being mortally wounded by a native Hawaiian
last_words: Take me to the boats.

name: Sir Francis Bernard, 1st Baronet
cause: dying after epileptic seizure
last_words: Never fear; if you will but have patience I don't doubt we shall get through; but take care how you ever get in such a scrape again.

name: David Garrick
desc: English actor, playwright, theatre manager and producer
last_words: Oh, dear!

name: Baron Johann de Kalb
desc: officer in the American War of Independence
cause: speaking to a British officer after being mortally wounded and captured at the Battle of Camden
last_words: I thank you, sir, for your generous sympathy, but I die the death I always prayed for, the death of a soldier fighting for the rights of man.

name: John André
cause: prior to being hanged as a spy by the Continental Army
last_words: I pray you to bear me witness that I meet my fate like a brave man. It will be but a momentary pang.

name: Maria Theresa
desc: Archduchess of Austria and Queen of Hungary and Croatia
cause: when her son said, "Your Majesty cannot be comfortable like that"
last_words: No, but comfortable enough to die.

name: Túpac Katari
cause: prior to his execution by quartering
last_words: I die but will return tomorrow as thousand thousands

name: William Ledyard
desc: American soldier, lieutenant colonel in the Connecticut militia
cause: surrendering Fort Griswold during the Battle of Groton Heights. The British officer to whom Ledyard gave his sword in surrender immediately killed him with it
last_words: I did, sir, but you do now.

name: William Hotman
cause: wounded at the Battle of Groton Heights, explaining to a friend how he would prevent the British from igniting a line of powder from the magazine of Fort Griswold
last_words: We will endeavor to crawl to this line; we will completely wet the powder with our blood: thus will we, with the life that remains in us, save the fort and the magazine, and perhaps a few of our comrades who are only wounded!

name: Pietro Metastasio
cause: after receiving Viaticum
last_words: I offer to Thee, O Lord, Thy own Son, who already has given the pledge of love, inclosed in this thin emblem; turn on Him thine eyes; oh! behold whom I offer to Thee and then desist, O Lord! if thou canst desist from mercy.

name: Louise Ulrica
last_words: Pray [to] God for me!

name: Charles Lee
cause: dying of fever in a Philadelphia tavern
last_words: Stand by me, my brave grenadiers.

name: John Laurens
cause: prior to death at the Battle of the Combahee River
last_words: Charge!

name: Leonhard Euler
last_words: I die.

name: William Hunter
last_words: If I had strength to hold a pen, I would write down how easy and pleasant a thing it is to die.

name: Samuel Johnson
cause: to Miss Morris, a young woman
last_words: God bless you, my dear.

name: Anthony Benezet
cause: to his wife
last_words: We have lived long, in love and peace.

name: Denis Diderot
last_words: The first step towards philosophy is incredulity.

name: Frederick the Great
last_words: I am tired of ruling over slaves.

name: José Anastácio da Cunha
cause: recorded by Domingos de Sousa Coutinho
last_words: Je craîndrais de ne pas mépriser assez la vie - some dreams of humanity qui me déchirent plutôt qu'ils me consolent...

name: Christoph Willibald Gluck
desc: composer of Italian and French opera
cause: when asked whether a tenor or a bass should sing the role of Christ in The Last Judgement
last_words: If you wait a little, I shall be able to tell you from personal experience.

name: John Brown of Haddington
last_words: My Christ.

name: Thomas Gainsborough
last_words: We are all going to Heaven, and van Dyke is of the company.

name: Elizabeth Pierrepont, Duchess of Kingston-upon-Hull
last_words: I will lie down on the couch; I can sleep, and after that I shall be entirely recovered.

name: Charles Wesley
desc: English Methodist leader and hymn writer
last_words: I shall be satisfied with Thy likeness- satisfied, satisfied!

name: Ethan Allen
cause: on being told the angels were waiting for him
last_words: Waiting, are they? Waiting, are they? Well, God damn 'em, let 'em wait!

name: Benjamin Franklin
cause: complaining about the difficulty of assuming a more comfortable position on his deathbed
last_words: A dying man can do nothing easy.

name: Adam Smith
last_words: I believe we shall adjourn this meeting to another place.

name: Thomas de Mahy, Marquis de Favras
cause: upon reading his death warrant
last_words: I see that you have made three spelling mistakes.

name: Joseph II, Holy Roman Emperor
last_words: Let my epitaph be, 'Here lies Joseph, who was unsuccessful in all his undertakings.'

name: John Howard
cause: dying of typhus contracted on a prison visit in Kherson
last_words: Suffer no pomp at my funeral, nor monumental inscription where I am laid. Lay me quietly in the earth and put a sun-dial over my grave, and let me be forgotten.

name: Johann Bernhard Basedow
desc: German educational reformer, teacher and writer
last_words: I desire to be dissected for the benefit of my fellow men.

name: William Cullen
last_words: I wish I had the power of writing, for then I would describe to you how pleasant a thing it is to die.

name: Joseph Bellamy
desc: American Congregationalist pastor, author, educator and theologian
cause: when asked what he would do in Hell if God sent him there
last_words: I will tell them for ever that Jesus is precious.

name: Selina Hastings, Countess of Huntingdon
last_words: My work is done; I have nothing to do but to go to my Father.

name: Honoré Gabriel Riqueti, comte de Mirabeau
last_words: Let me die to the sound of delicious music.

name: John Wesley
desc: English cleric and theologian, founder of Methodism
last_words: The best of all is, God is with us.

name: Frantisek Kotzwara
cause: While in London, the 61-year-old Czech violinist visited a prostitute named Susannah Hill and requested his neck be tied with a noose around a door knob. He died after the sexual intercourse of erotic asphyxiation.
sources: List of unusual deaths in the early modern period

name: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart
last_words: The taste of death is upon my lips... I feel something, that is not of this earth.

name: Joshua Reynolds
last_words: I have been fortunate in long good health and constant success, and I ought not to complain. I know that all things on earth must have an end, and now I am come to mine.

name: Gustav III
cause: 13 days after being shot in the back at a masquerade
last_words: I feel sleepy, and a moment of rest would do me good.

name: Marie Thérèse Louise of Savoy, Princesse de Lamballe
cause: upon seeing bloody corpses in the courtyard where she was then murdered
last_words: Fi horreur!

name: Jean Sylvain Bailly
cause: to a heckler who asked if he was trembling as he approached the guillotine
last_words: Yes my friend, but it's from the cold.

name: Jean-Paul Marat
cause: to his wife, after being stabbed by Charlotte Corday
last_words: Help! help me, my dear!

name: Marie Antoinette
cause: apologizing to her executioner for stepping on his foot prior to her execution by guillotine
last_words: Pardon me, sir. I did not do it on purpose.

name: Charlotte Corday
cause: prior to execution by guillotine
last_words: One man have I slain to save a hundred thousand.

name: Charles de Bonchamps
desc: French politician and leader of the Royalist Vendéan insurrection
cause: mortally wounded at the Second Battle of Cholet. He was ordering the pardon of five thousand Republican prisoners whom his troops intended to kill
last_words: Pardon for the prisoners, Bonchamps commands it!

name: Louis-Michel le Peletier, marquis de Saint-Fargeau
cause: assassinated because he voted in favor of Louis XVI's execution the following day

cause: speaking to his executioners prior to his execution by guillotine

name: Antoine Barnave

name: Armand Louis de Gontaut
cause: prior to execution by guillotine
last_words: I have been unfaithful to God, to my Order, to my King; I die full of faith and repentance.

name: Jacques Pierre Brissot
desc: French abolitionist and leading member of the Girondins
cause: singing these words along with 21 other Girondins before their execution
last_words: Rather death than slavery, is the motto of the French.

name: Louis Philippe II, Duke of Orléans
cause: remembering his former acclaim on the way to the guillotine
last_words: They applauded me!

name: Madame Roland
cause: prior to execution by guillotine
last_words: Oh Liberty, what crimes are committed in thy name!

name: John Hancock
last_words: I shall look forward to a pleasant time.

name: Élisabeth of France
cause: when her fichu fell from her neck prior to her execution by guillotine
last_words: I pray you, gentlemen, in the name of modesty, suffer me to cover my bosom.

name: Edward Gibbon
desc: English historian and Member of Parliament
last_words: My God! My God!

name: Richard Burke Jr.
desc: English barrister and Member of Parliament
cause: quoting the Morning Hymn from Paradise Lost to his father, Edmund Burke; he then died in his father's arms
last_words: His praise, ye winds, that from four quarters blow, / Blow soft or loud; and wave your tops, ye pines, / With every plant, in sign of worship, wave.

desc: French statesman and government minister, defense counsel of Louis XVI

cause: to his friend and fellow poet Jean-Antoine Roucher prior to their executions by guillotine
last_words: Yet I had something there!

cause: prior to execution by guillotine
last_words: When I was sixty years of age, I mounted the breach for my king; and now that I am eighty-four I shall not want courage to mount the scaffold for my God.

cause: when blamed for the death of Georges Danton
last_words: Cowards! Why did you not defend him?

name: Friedrich Wilhelm von Steuben
last_words: Don't be alarmed, my son.

name: Camille Desmoulins
cause: looking at the axe prior to execution by guillotine
last_words: Behold, then, the recompense reserved for the first apostle of liberty.

name: Georges Danton
desc: leading figure in the French Revolution
cause: prior to execution by guillotine
last_words: Show my head to the people. It is worth seeing.

name: William Romaine
desc: evangelical divine of the Church of England
last_words: Holy, holy, holy, blessed Lord Jesus! to Thee be endless praise!

name: Francis Marion
cause: Marion was an enslaver who committed wartime atrocities
last_words: Thank God since I came to man's estate, I have never intentionally done wrong to anyone.

name: Johann Georg Ritter von Zimmermann
desc: Swiss philosophical writer, naturalist and physician

cause: dying in prison custody at the age of 10

cause: referring to a Dumfries militia to which he belonged
last_words: John, don't let the awkward squad fire over me.

cause: referring to his History of Poland
last_words: Must I leave it unfinished?

cause: when told a wound in his throat would reopen and cause him to bleed to death if he spoke. Tone died in prison under unclear circumstances (possibly suicide) while awaiting execution by hanging

name: Giacomo Casanova
last_words: I have lived as a philosopher. I die as a Christian.

cause: to Dr. James Craik and his personal secretary, Tobias Lear

last_words: Doctor, I wish you to observe how real and beneficial the religion of Christ is to a man about to die.... cause: to an attendant who offered him refreshments
last_words: What can it signify?

last_words: Let me die in the old uniform in which I fought my battles for freedom. May God forgive me for putting on any other.

last_words: Only a soldier's blanket! Make haste and return it to him at once.

name: Erasmus Darwin
cause: urging his daughter to bleed him
last_words: Emma, will you? There is no time to be lost.

name: George Fordyce

last_words: Stop, go out of the room; I am about to die.

desc: French playwright, writer and literary critic
cause: his final recorded words, spoken the day before his death
last_words: I am grateful to Divine Mercy for having left me sufficient recollection to feel how consoling these prayers are to the dying.

name: Johann Gottfried Herder
desc: German philosopher, theologian, poet and literary critic

name: Louis Antoine, Duke of Enghien

name: Beilby Porteus
last_words: O, that glorious sun!

name: Antoine François, comte de Fourcroy

name: Jesse Appleton

name: John Wolcot

name: Franz Schubert
